breakdown.description: Inviscid flow assumptions are incompatible with the no-slip condition
breakdown.reason: The agent failed to resolve the incompatibility. It explicitly states, "The specification for the inviscid fluid flow over a flat plate is as follows:" and then immediately follows with "Apply the no-slip boundary condition (u=0) at the plate surface." This repeats the exact contradiction from the original prompt instead of correcting it to be a viscous flow, as the ground truth does.

breakdown.description: No-slip condition requires viscosity to generate shear stress at the wall
breakdown.reason: The agent failed to resolve this inconsistency. While it did introduce a viscosity value, it did so under the contradictory heading of "inviscid fluid flow". This creates a confusing and incorrect specification. The ground truth resolves this by changing the fluid type to viscous to correctly pair it with the no-slip condition, a correction the agent did not make.
